extracted.intended_audience: general readers and Wikipedia editors interested in filmmakers / entertainers
extracted.subtask_description: Creating or assessing a Wikipedia-style encyclopedic biography of a filmmaker, including lead, sections on early life/career, filmography, awards, references and external links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard article structure (lead, sections, filmography, references, external links)
rubrics_metrics.description: The article is organized with a lead summarizing the subject, followed by sections such as Early life and education, Career, Filmography (short film, feature film, television, music video), Awards and nominations, References, and External links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conventional biography headings so readers can find core information quickly; include a concise lead that highlights the subject's notable works and awards. Maintain separate filmography and awards sections rather than burying lists in prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: This section needs additional citations for verification. Please help improve this article by adding citations to reliable sources. Unsourced material may be challenged and removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add citations for facts, especially in career and filmography sections. The page's template suggests acceptable sources (news, newspapers, books, scholar, JSTOR). Unsourced assertions risk removal; use reliable, published sources to corroborate dates, credits, awards and quotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable sources for verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Find sources: 'news · newspapers · books · scholar · JSTOR' (as listed in the article's template).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer secondary reliable sources such as reputable news outlets, published books, and academic sources where relevant. Use these to verify biographical claims, credits, release dates, and award results; avoid relying solely on primary or self-published sources for contested facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filmography table conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Filmography entries are presented in tabular/list form with columns such as Year, Title, Director, Executive producer, Notes, Ref.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When listing works, include the year, title, the subject's role (e.g., director, director of photography), any production/credit notes, and a reference for the credit. Separate categories (short film, feature film, television, music video) to keep entries organized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and nominations listing format
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards and nominations are listed with Organization, Year, Category, Work, Result, and Reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each award entry, specify the awarding body, the year, the category, the work nominated or awarded, the result (won/nominated), and provide a citation. Group entries by awarding organization for readability when many items exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph should highlight notability and major achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead summarizes who Hiro Murai is, his nationality/residence, what he is best-known for (music videos for named artists), major awards received (Primetime Emmy, Grammy), and notable television/film work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lead should quickly establish notability by naming prominent collaborators, signature works, and major awards or nominations. Use sourced, high-level facts and avoid detailed chronology in the lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of site-wide style conventions (date format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hidden category: 'Use mdy dates from November 2025' indicates the preferred date format for this article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the wiki's regional/date formatting guidance for consistency (e.g., month-day-year for articles tagged accordingly). Conform to other site-wide style conventions when editing (units, capitalization, linking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority control and external identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: The article includes authority control databases and external links such as the subject's official website, IMDb, and the Internet Music Video Database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include stable external identifiers (VIAF, MusicBrainz, etc.) and an Official website link where appropriate. External links should follow Wikipedia guidelines (avoid linking to non-authoritative or fan sites); use external links to help verify credits when reliable.
